My roommate and I took mushrooms in our student flat on a Friday night. Neither of us had much experience. We'd each eaten about 2.5g. For the first hour we were laughing a lot. Then he went quiet and said he felt like his heart was doing something weird. I looked at him and his face started to look grey and sick, and I got scared that he was having a heart attack. He saw that I was scared, and that made him more scared. Within minutes we were both in full panic, feeding off each other. He was pacing up and down saying 'I'm dying, I'm dying', and I was sitting on the floor convinced that I was going to have to watch my best friend die and that it would be my fault because I bought the mushrooms.

Then my own body started doing things. My hands went numb and tingly, my chest got tight, and I thought maybe the mushrooms were poisonous and we were both dying. I looked up poisonous mushrooms on my phone and the pictures made everything worse. The walls were breathing and the light from the phone screen was burning my eyes.

I called my mum. It was 1am. I was crying and I told her we'd taken mushrooms and were dying. She stayed calm somehow, and told me to put my roommate on the phone too, and she talked to us both for over an hour, telling us to breathe, asking us silly questions about what we could see. She said if anything got worse she would call an ambulance, and she checked on us every ten minutes after we hung up. My dad drove three hours that night to come get me. I was so ashamed when he arrived. He didn't say much, he just made us toast and tea and sat with us until morning.

Ich war mit Freunden in einem Club in Berlin und hatte LSD genommen. Ich bin irgendwann allein durch den Club gelaufen und in einen Bereich geraten, wo viele Leute halbnackt waren und Sex hatten. Ich war völlig überfordert, alles war laut, dunkel und eng, und ich fand den Ausgang nicht. Fremde Menschen haben mich angefasst. Ich hatte das Gefühl, in der Hölle zu sein, und konnte nicht atmen. Irgendwann hat mich ein Türsteher rausgeführt.

I'm a mother of two. My husband and I don't get much time to ourselves, and for our tenth anniversary we went to a cabin for the weekend and left the kids with my sister. We'd both done mushrooms a couple of times in college and decided to do it again, a moderate dose, maybe 2 grams each.

About an hour in, while we were sitting by the fire and feeling lovely, my phone rang. It was my sister. My younger son, who's three, had a high fever and was having what she thought was a seizure. She was panicking. She said she was calling an ambulance.

I can't describe what that did to me. I couldn't think. The words she was saying were coming apart. I was trying to understand what was happening to my son and my mind was full of colours and shapes and the fire was crackling and it all felt like a nightmare. I kept asking her to repeat things. My husband took the phone and he was in a similar state. We couldn't drive. We were two hours away. We were completely useless to our child, who needed us.

Then the visions started. I saw my son's little body, blue and still. I saw a small coffin. I saw myself at a funeral, and everyone was looking at me, knowing that I had been off taking drugs while my son died. I felt that this was a punishment, that the universe was showing me what kind of mother I really was. I was on the floor of the cabin, sobbing and screaming. My husband tried to hold me but he was crying too.

My sister called again about forty minutes later from the hospital. It was a febrile seizure, which I now know is quite common and usually harmless, and my son was okay. But in that state I didn't believe her. I thought she was lying to protect me. I kept saying 'tell me the truth'. I asked her to put him on the phone and he was asleep, so I couldn't hear him, and my mind filled in the worst.

The rest of the night I sat by the window waiting for the drugs to wear off so we could drive. Every minute felt like an hour. I kept seeing the coffin. We left at 6am and drove straight to the hospital. When I finally held my son, he was sleepy and cranky and completely fine, and I couldn't stop shaking.

My sister was kind about it but I know she was shocked when we told her. I've never felt so much shame in my life.

I bought what I thought was LSD from a dealer at a party. It turned out later it was probably 25I-NBOMe. It tasted bitter, which should have warned me. About an hour later my hands and feet went ice cold and turned bluish, my heart was racing and my jaw was clenched. I started shaking uncontrollably and my vision went very weird, everything pixelated and pulsing. I was terrified, I thought I was being poisoned. My friends called an ambulance. In the hospital they gave me benzos and I remember the doctor saying something about vasoconstriction. I was in the ER all night and very confused.

Ich habe an einer Psilocybin-Studie für Menschen mit therapieresistenter Depression teilgenommen. Ich hatte große Hoffnungen. Die Sitzung fand in einem gemütlich eingerichteten Raum in der Klinik statt, mit zwei Begleitern. Ich bekam eine hohe Dosis.

Nach etwa einer Stunde fühlte ich mich, als würde ich in einen dunklen Schacht fallen. Alles, was ich an Hoffnung mitgebracht hatte, war weg. Ich sah mein Leben als eine endlose Kette von Versagen und Enttäuschungen. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass meine Depression nicht eine Krankheit ist, sondern die Wahrheit über mich. Dass ich eben ein Mensch bin, der nicht glücklich sein kann.

Dann kam das Gefühl, eingesperrt zu sein. Der Raum wurde enger. Die Musik, die eigentlich beruhigend sein sollte, klang wie eine Totenmesse. Ich wollte die Augenmaske abnehmen und aufstehen, aber ich hatte das Gefühl, dass ich mich nicht bewegen kann. Ich hörte die Stimmen der Begleiter, aber sie klangen weit weg und gleichgültig.

Die Begleiter haben mich nicht allein gelassen, das muss ich sagen. Eine von ihnen hat meine Hand gehalten und immer wieder gesagt, dass ich sicher bin. Aber ich konnte das nicht fühlen. Das ging vielleicht drei Stunden so. Gegen Ende wurde es etwas leichter, und ich hatte einen kurzen Moment, in dem ich die Hand der Begleiterin wirklich gespürt habe, als etwas Warmes. Das war der einzige Lichtblick.
LSD and alcohol at a party. I blacked out parts of the night. I remember screaming at my boyfriend and him crying, and waking up on the bathroom floor. I still don't know everything that happened.

I took a high dose of mushrooms, about 5 grams, at home with my partner. It was my idea, I'd read about 'heroic doses'. She took a smaller dose to look after me.

About an hour and a half in, I looked at her and something was wrong. She looked exactly like her, but I knew with absolute certainty that it wasn't her. It was someone, or something, wearing her face. Her movements were slightly off, her voice was slightly wrong, like a recording. I tried to stay calm and test her. I asked her questions only she would know. She answered them correctly, which made it worse, because it meant the impostor had access to her memories. I started thinking that the real her was somewhere else, maybe dead, and this thing had taken her place.

I locked myself in the bedroom with our cat. The cat was the only thing I trusted. I sat in the corner holding him and listening to her knocking on the door and calling my name, and every time I heard her voice I felt sick with fear. I was also sure the thing could change shape and might come through the walls. I could see the walls bulging.

She called my brother, who came over. I didn't trust him either. They talked to me through the door for hours. Eventually I fell asleep, or passed out, holding the cat.

The next morning I woke up and the drug had worn off, but the feeling hadn't fully gone. I looked at her and I knew in my head it was her, but there was a tiny voice saying 'are you sure?'. That voice lasted for days. I couldn't kiss her. I'd test her with questions. She was very hurt and scared. My brother took me to a doctor on the third day.

Ich habe mit einer Freundin an einer Ayahuasca-Zeremonie in Kolumbien teilgenommen. Wir waren etwa zehn Leute in einer Hütte. Während der Zeremonie habe ich gesehen, wie der Schamane zu einer jungen Frau gegangen ist, die neben mir lag, und sie auf eine Weise angefasst hat, die nicht in Ordnung war. Sie hat sich weggedreht, aber er hat weitergemacht. Ich wollte etwas sagen, aufstehen, eingreifen, aber ich war wie gelähmt. Mein Körper hat mir nicht gehorcht. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass er mich ansieht und dass ich die Nächste bin. Ich habe stundenlang in der Dunkelheit gelegen, voller Angst und Scham, dass ich nichts getan habe.
Ego death on 5 grams. Thought I would never come back to being a person.

I smoked changa in a chill-out tent at a festival. Someone said it was 'gentle DMT'. It wasn't gentle. I was pulled up through a tunnel of colours and came into a space where there were tall beings made of light standing in a circle around me. They seemed to be waiting for me to say something, and I didn't know what. I felt a terrible responsibility, as if I was failing a test that I didn't know I was taking. Then they turned away from me, all at once, and I felt cast out, rejected by the universe itself. I came back and immediately burst into tears. I cried for hours in the tent and nobody really knew what to do. For the rest of the festival, whenever I closed my eyes I saw the tunnel and felt like I was being pulled back.

Ich war auf einem Microdosing-Retreat, bei dem auch intensive Atemarbeit gemacht wurde. Während der Atemübung bekam ich eine heftige Panikattacke, habe hyperventiliert, meine Hände haben sich verkrampft und ich konnte sie nicht mehr bewegen. Die Leiterin hat gesagt, ich solle einfach weiteratmen. Ich hatte Todesangst.

I am a gay man from a country where homosexuality is not accepted, and where drug use is punished harshly. I'll leave the country unnamed. At the time of this experience I was living in the capital, very much in the closet at work and with my family. My boyfriend and I had a small apartment that we said we shared as 'friends'.

A friend who'd lived in Europe brought back some LSD and gave us two tabs. We waited for a weekend when we had nothing planned and took them at home. For a few hours it was the most beautiful experience. We felt free, we danced, we laughed, we held each other. For the first time in my life I felt completely accepted as I am.

Then, in the evening, we heard loud banging on the door. Police. Later I found out that our neighbour had heard music and two men's voices, and had been suspicious of us for a long time. I was at the peak of the trip. The banging sounded like the end of the world. My boyfriend tried to hide the remaining tabs. I opened the door because I thought that if I didn't, they would break it.

Four officers came in. They saw how we looked, our pupils, and they knew immediately. They searched the apartment and found the foil with the tabs. They found photos on my phone of me and my boyfriend. One of them started shouting the word they use for gay men, and hit my boyfriend in the face. I froze. The colours were still moving, the officers' faces were melting and turning into animal faces. I didn't know if this was real or if I had gone insane.

They handcuffed us and took us to the police station in separate cars. I sat in the back of the car and watched the city lights stream past like rivers of blood. In the station they put me in a small room with one bare bulb. The bulb was pulsing. I was alone for what felt like days. Then two officers came in and interrogated me. They wanted names: who gave us the drugs, who else was gay, who else was in our circle. When I didn't answer, one of them slapped me repeatedly. They threatened to call my family and my employer. They said I would go to prison for years and that I'd be raped there. I was still tripping and I believed everything they said, more than believed, I saw it happening.

At some point I lost myself completely. There was no more me, just fear and the bulb and the voices. I think I gave them some names. I don't remember. That's one of the things I can't forgive myself for.

We were held for two days. My boyfriend had a broken nose. A cousin of mine who is a lawyer got us out. I don't know what he paid. My family found out about everything. My father didn't speak to me for a year.

Three months later, my boyfriend and I left the country. We applied for asylum in Europe. That's where I'm living now.
